what_changed: Generalisation erosion continues: OOD_DEV 0.726 (1,800) -> 0.663 -> 0.625 while ID stays 0.999; interaction 0.355 -> 0.397; IIT warm-up reached its full strength (lambda = 3 at step 2,000); editability steady (0.91), copy 0.998; weight motion back to small (<= 0.07).
hypothesis: After convergence, continued training (now at full IIT strength) keeps fitting the familiar unit-value combinations with a lookup-like upstream binding and moves the network away from the configuration that best handled held-out combinations (peak at 1,700-1,800); the rising interaction is part of that drift.
evidence: Observation: OOD_DEV trajectory 0.68 (1,500), 0.64, 0.72, 0.73, 0.66, 0.63 with ID ~1.0 throughout; upstream weight motion at 1,900 coincided with the largest drop. Correlational: interaction rising alongside. Causal: the 1,500 and 1,800 dry runs show that registered interaction-reducing edits do NOT restore generalisation (they cost 0.017-0.026).
key_question: Is the erosion transient (OOD recovers, as accuracy did after the 1,600 spike) or a monotone trend to the end of training?
best_experiment: Keep recording OOD_DEV for A (= B) at every checkpoint; if it keeps falling, the strongest evidence-based remedy is a checkpoint-anchored upstream regulariser (pull attn1/attn2 toward the best-OOD_DEV checkpoint, i.e. per-tensor early stopping chosen on the development split) -- proposed as a future primitive, NOT registered here.
intervention_rationale: The defect is real, but the registered primitives were shown (1,500, 1,800) to worsen it; the remedies that match the diagnosis (layer-1 binding supervision; checkpoint anchoring) are not registered and per the spec cannot be added to the active pilot.
